newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-FAVORITES CRUZEIRO AND GUARANI SOUNDLY BEATEN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FAVORITES CRUZEIRO AND GUARANI SOUNDLY BEATEN.

text.p: Cruzeiro and Guarani, who finished first and second respectively in the first stage of the Brazilian championship, were both soundly beaten in their quarter-final, first leg games on Wednesday.
A tired-looking Cruzeiro, playing their 78th competitive game this year, were beaten 3-0 away by Portuguesa while Guarani lost 3-1 away to Goias.
Portuguesa, who sneaked into the last eight on Sunday when they won and the two teams above them both lost, dominated their game and could have added to their tally.

Striker Rodrigo, one of Brazilian soccer's most impressive revelations this year, opened the scoring in the fifth minute of injury time at the end of the first half of a game which started an hour late due to a power failure in Sao Paulo.
Two goals by substitute Alex Alves in a five minute spell in the second half buried Cruzeiro, who had defender Celio Lucio sent off for wildly kicking at an opponent.

Cruzeiro, from the city of Belo Horizonte, are one of Brazilian soccer's traditional powers, having won the South American Libertadores Cup once and the Supercup twice. However, they have never won the Brazilian championship.

This year they have also taken part in the Copa Brasil, which they won, the Supercup, where they have reached the final, as well as the Brazilian championship and a regional competition, which they also won.
However, their season looks set for a frustrating end as last Wednesday they were beaten 1-0 at home by Argentina's Velez Sarsfield in the first leg of the Supercup final.

Guarani, where volatile president Beto Zini has made headlines by employing ten coaches this year, were sunk by two goals scored by Goias striker Alex. The second legs are at the weekend with aggregate score deciding the ties.
